obligations.behavior: a replace keeps the id with a new sha256 and GET/file serve the new bytes with one updated event; a wrong-kind key gets 403 forbidden_kind and nothing changes; a todo .md upload succeeds on an old-schema store
obligations.source_text: All 3 acceptance criteria from issue #10 pass as automated tests: (1) a replace returns the same id with a new sha256, GET /{id} and /file serve the new bytes, and the feed has exactly 1 new 'updated' event; (2) a key without the item's kind gets 403 forbidden_kind with the item's sha256 unchanged; (3) POST kind=todo with a .md file returns 201 on a database created with the old 9-kind schema.

obligations.behavior: replace refuses what upload refuses with the same codes and changes nothing
obligations.source_text: A new write route PUT /api/library/{id}/file (multipart 'file') replaces an item's bytes and keeps its id: it runs the same caps and format/content checks as upload (ingest._validate + _check_content), writes the new blob before commit, and UPDATEs sha256, size and format. No such route exists today (routes_library.py has GET/POST/GET id/GET file/DELETE/restore at 203-376) and no store method updates bytes.

obligations.behavior: search finds the new body and not the old; index_queue row is pending, attempts 0
obligations.source_text: Replace re-indexes the item the way index_on_add does. search.set_body rewrites the FTS row (keyed rowid = item.id) inside the transaction. The index_queue row resets to pending, mirroring requeue_* (indexer.py:106-134), because enqueue is INSERT OR IGNORE and would do nothing. _notify_indexer wakes the embedder. Stale embeddings are keyed by item_id and the indexer replaces them.

obligations.behavior: one updated event with the new sha256 and replace data, in the same transaction; same bytes is a no-op
obligations.source_text: Replace appends an 'updated' feed event carrying the NEW sha256, built from the updated item. The data field is {replaced: true, old_sha256, size, format}, so Gwen's reconcile on (id, sha256) sees the change. 'updated' is already in EVENT_TYPES (feed.py:20), and restore already uses _event(conn, 'updated', item, {restored: true}) (library.py:205, 398).

obligations.behavior: a key that cannot write the item's kind gets 403 forbidden_kind before any bytes change
obligations.source_text: Replace is authorized exactly like restore: _writable() (routes_library.py:354-358) runs check(write), then library.get(include_archived=True), then check(write, item.kind). A key that cannot write the item's kind gets 403 {code: forbidden_kind} from auth.check (auth.py:182-192), and the item is left unchanged.

obligations.behavior: bytes owned by another item give 409 duplicate_content, never IntegrityError, never leaking a hidden id
obligations.source_text: New bytes whose sha256 already belongs to ANOTHER item are refused with 409 and a dedicated machine code (not the opaque 'conflict'), checked before the UPDATE so the UNIQUE constraint (store.py:36) never raises IntegrityError. When the other item is private and the caller cannot see it, the response stays opaque and gives no id, as the existing ConflictError/CONFLICT_DETAIL does (library.py:136-141).

obligations.behavior: todo is a kind and keys mint --kind todo works
obligations.source_text: 'todo' is added to KINDS (models.py:12-22). Everything that derives from KINDS picks it up with no other edit: library.check_kind, feed.append, keys.mint validation (keys.py:168; the CLI --kind has no choices=), the MCP kind enum (mcp/tools.py:23), the search Literal (routes_search.py:111), OPDS and WebDAV folders. 'culture-library keys mint --kind todo' then works, and md is already a supported format (ingest.py:56).

obligations.behavior: an old DB migrates once, keeping ids, column order and child rows; racing opens rebuild once
obligations.source_text: On open, an idempotent schema migration rebuilds the items table so its kind CHECK matches the current KINDS on an existing database. It detects drift from sqlite_master.sql, keeps every id, the sqlite_sequence/AUTOINCREMENT high-water mark, the column order (test_items_columns asserts it) and the child rows (embeddings, index_queue). It runs on an old backup restored later too, because backup.restore copies the DB verbatim and never opens a Store (backup.py:296-312).

The migration runs on a dedicated connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF set BEFORE its BEGIN IMMEDIATE, never inside Store.connect(). SQLite ignores that pragma inside a transaction, and connect() always begins one (store.py:89-106), so a rebuild there would cascade-delete every embeddings and index_queue row. After taking the write lock it re-reads sqlite_master and rebuilds only if the CHECK is still stale, because a second process (e.g. 'docker compose exec library culture-library keys mint', keys.py:27 builds its own Store) can race the server's first open. It runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check before COMMIT.

obligations.behavior: no purged id is reissued after migration
obligations.source_text: The migration carries sqlite_sequence's items value across the rebuild explicitly. The textbook create/copy/drop/rename resets it to max(id), so after a purge the next upload REUSES a purged id, and purged ids are already published as 'purged' feed events that consumers reconcile by id.

obligations.behavior: a lossy rebuild rolls back and refuses to open; success logs one line
obligations.source_text: The migration verifies itself before COMMIT: the items row count, max(id) and the embeddings/index_queue child counts must equal their pre-rebuild values, or it rolls back and raises (the store does not open). On success it writes one diagnostic line to stderr naming the old and new kind sets and the row count.

obligations.behavior: after any interleaving of replaces, every live item's blob exists and hashes correctly
obligations.source_text: Replace makes sure the new blob exists INSIDE its write transaction (write it if missing), as on_insert and _reuse_existing already do (library.py:197-198, 237-238). Unlinking unreferenced old blobs makes a toggle-back race real: unchecking a line restores an earlier checklist's exact bytes, so a concurrent replace can unlink a blob another replace wrote before it took the lock.

obligations.behavior: the cited upload copy and existing push tests pass unchanged; a new replace contract test exists
obligations.source_text: tests/contract/culture_rules_wire.py stays a byte-for-byte cited copy of culture-rules' library.push (test_cited_copy_matches_upstream). The replace route's culture-rules contract goes in a separate new test, and the existing upload behaviour (201, then 200 on dedupe, plus the error codes) does not change.
WebDAV stays read-only. routes_webdav.py answers 405 to PUT and every other write method (lines 6-7, 41-43, 138), so the HTTP replace route is the only new write path.

A replace changes only the bytes and the fields derived from them (sha256, size, format). title, author, kind, visibility, created_at and the uploader record stay as they are. Title is never extracted from content (ingest.py:420-421 uses the filename stem or the supplied title), so keeping it is consistent.

obligations.behavior: a todo item can be created, replaced under the same id, and its key minted
obligations.source_text: culture-rules PUTs new Markdown bytes to /api/library/{id}/file and gets the same id back with a new sha256. GET /api/library/{id} and /file serve the new bytes, and /api/feed shows an 'updated' event for that id. A todo item uploads on the migrated live database, and 'culture-library keys mint --kind todo' mints a key that can write it.

obligations.behavior: the live library migrates in place 51/51 with ids unchanged
obligations.source_text: The live library on spark migrates in place with 51 of 51 items, 0 lost, every id unchanged, and the full suite and CI stay green (coverage >= 60%).

obligations.behavior: the runbook's steps are followed for the live upgrade and counts filed
obligations.source_text: docs/operations/deploy.md gains an upgrade procedure for schema-changing releases: run 'culture-library backup' and verify it, deploy the new image, check the one-line migration diagnostic in the container logs, and compare SELECT count(*), max(id) FROM items with the pre-upgrade values.

obligations.behavior: the rebuild behaves on the image's SQLite as on the host's
obligations.source_text: The rebuild procedure behaves the same on the deployed image's SQLite 3.40.1 (python:3.12-slim-bookworm) as on the host's 3.45.1 that runs the tests. RENAME and foreign_key_check semantics have been stable since 3.26, but nothing in CI runs the migration on 3.40.
